scope: Corollary 6.2 (From bounded coset densities to Fourier decay) of the manuscript “Random coordinate frames and partial permutation laws” (preprints/Random-coordinate-frames-and-partial-permutation-laws-September-26-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 238 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 0a520da2d4a92a17), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 20. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let a finite set X be partitioned into k > 18 nonempty sets M1, . . . , Mk, and put G = Sym(X). Let Ha be the subgroup that permutes Ma and fixes X \ Ma pointwise. Suppose that a probability measure ν on G satisfies, for some B ≥ 1, ν(gHa) ≤ B |Ha| |G| (g ∈ G, 1 ≤ a ≤ k). Then every irreducible complex unitary representation ρ of G, of dimension D, satisfies ∥b ν(ρ)∥op ≤ p kBC0 D−(1−18/k)/2 . (6.10) Here C0 is the absolute constant of Lemma 6.1. The block sizes need not be equal.
